difficultyReason: Two-step causal chain (new filtration policy → reduced contaminant levels → improved public health outcomes). The weakener attacks the move from reduced contaminants to improved health by introducing an alternative explanation for the health data. Distractors include a strengthener and an out-of-scope fact about filtration technology.
stimulus: A municipal water authority installed a new filtration system three years ago, after which measurements showed a 30 percent decline in waterborne contaminant levels in the city's tap water. Over the same period, rates of gastrointestinal illness among city residents dropped by 22 percent. The authority concluded that the filtration system was responsible for the reduction in illness.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new filtration system cost significantly more to operate than the system it replaced.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the same three-year period, a citywide public health campaign successfully increased handwashing compliance rates by 40 percent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Waterborne contaminants are known to cause gastrointestinal illness in laboratory studies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new filtration system also reduced levels of heavy metals in the city's tap water.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Several neighboring municipalities that did not install new filtration systems reported no change in gastrointestinal illness rates over the same period.

explanations.correct: The argument concludes that the filtration system caused the drop in gastrointestinal illness. Choice B introduces a competing cause—a handwashing campaign that also occurred during the same period and independently could have reduced gastrointestinal illness rates. This alternative explanation undermines the authority's causal attribution to the filtration system.
explanations.A: Out-of-scope trap. Operating costs are irrelevant to whether the filtration system caused the health improvement. This does not touch the premise-to-conclusion move.
explanations.B: Correct. Introduces an alternative explanation for the decline in illness, attacking the causal link between the filtration system and improved health outcomes.
explanations.C: Opposite-answer (strengthener) trap. Confirming that waterborne contaminants cause gastrointestinal illness in lab settings actually bolsters the argument's assumption that reduced contaminants should reduce illness.
explanations.D: Too narrow / irrelevant trap. That the system reduced heavy metals is a tangential benefit; it does not address the causal relationship between the filtration system and gastrointestinal illness specifically.
explanations.E: Shift-in-subject trap. The comparison with municipalities that did not upgrade is ambiguous at best and could even be read as supporting the argument by suggesting that without new filtration, no improvement occurred—making this a mild strengthener rather than a weakener.

difficultyReason: Predictive argument: an economist uses historical correlation between consumer confidence index rises and GDP growth to predict that a current confidence surge will produce GDP growth. The weakener attacks the premise-to-conclusion move by identifying a structural difference that makes the historical pattern inapplicable now. Distractors include a strengthener and an irrelevant statistic.
stimulus: An economist noted that over the past four decades, every time the national consumer confidence index rose by more than 10 points in a single quarter, GDP growth of at least 2 percent followed within 12 months. The consumer confidence index has now risen by 14 points this quarter. The economist therefore predicts that GDP growth of at least 2 percent will occur within the next 12 months.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the economist's prediction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consumer confidence indices are calculated using survey data collected from a random sample of households.

choices.label: B
choices.text: GDP growth of 2 percent is generally considered the minimum threshold for a healthy economy by most financial analysts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The current surge in consumer confidence is driven entirely by anticipated government subsidies that economists expect will be canceled before consumers can increase their actual spending.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In all four decades studied, the rises in consumer confidence were accompanied by low unemployment rates, which also independently predict GDP growth.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Consumer confidence has risen by more than 10 points in a single quarter on six separate occasions over the past four decades.

explanations.correct: The economist's prediction rests on the assumption that past correlations hold because rising confidence translates into increased consumer spending, which drives GDP. Choice C reveals that the current confidence rise is based on anticipated subsidies expected to be canceled, meaning actual spending—and thus GDP impact—will not follow. This attacks the mechanism linking the confidence index to GDP growth, undermining the prediction.
explanations.A: Out-of-scope trap. The methodology for calculating the index does not bear on whether the historical correlation holds or whether the current situation differs meaningfully from past instances.
explanations.B: Irrelevant trap. What analysts consider a healthy growth threshold is a definitional point that neither strengthens nor weakens the prediction about whether that growth will occur.
explanations.C: Correct. Identifies a structural difference between current conditions and all historical instances, severing the link between confidence and actual economic activity.
explanations.D: This actually weakens the argument, but less directly than C—it suggests the confidence index may be a spurious correlate rather than a cause, since low unemployment (not present in the current situation) may have been doing the real work. However, the stimulus does not specify current unemployment, making this weaker than C's direct attack on the spending mechanism. On the LSAT, C is the stronger, more targeted weakener.
explanations.E: Accurate-but-irrelevant trap. Stating how many times confidence rose in the historical sample simply restates background information consistent with the economist's premise and does nothing to weaken the prediction.

difficultyReason: Analogical argument: a policy advocate argues that because a literacy program reduced recidivism in one jurisdiction, an identical program should reduce recidivism in a second jurisdiction. The weakener attacks the analogy by identifying a relevant disanalogy. Distractors include a strengthener, a premise-level attack that leaves the conclusion standing, and an out-of-scope comparison.
stimulus: A policy advocate argued that a voluntary prison literacy program introduced in Westfield County reduced inmate recidivism rates by 18 percent over five years. She therefore recommended that Hartley County adopt an identical program, predicting it would achieve comparable reductions in recidivism there.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the advocate's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Westfield County literacy program was funded primarily through private donations rather than public tax revenue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Studies in organizational behavior show that voluntary programs consistently attract participants who are already more motivated to reform than the general prison population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hartley County's prison population has a substantially higher proportion of inmates serving sentences for violent offenses, a group for which literacy interventions have shown little effect on recidivism.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Westfield County also expanded its post-release employment support services during the same five-year period in which the literacy program operated.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recidivism rates in Hartley County have remained unchanged for the past decade despite several other reform initiatives.

explanations.correct: The argument is analogical: because the program worked in Westfield County, it will work in Hartley County. Choice C identifies a relevant disanalogy—Hartley County's population is predominantly violent offenders, for whom literacy programs have not demonstrated effectiveness. This directly undermines the assumption that the two counties are sufficiently similar for the results to transfer.
explanations.A: Out-of-scope trap. Funding source (private vs. public) is irrelevant to whether the program achieves recidivism reductions. It might affect feasibility but does not bear on the advocate's causal or analogical reasoning.
explanations.B: This is a self-selection / methodological attack on the Westfield County finding itself—it suggests the 18 percent reduction may not have been caused by the program. However, it attacks a premise (the Westfield result) rather than the analogical move to Hartley County. Even if the Westfield finding is methodologically flawed, the same flaw would apply similarly in Hartley County, leaving the comparative recommendation somewhat intact. Choice C more directly attacks the conclusion.
explanations.C: Correct. Establishes a material disanalogy between the two jurisdictions that breaks the analogical inference at its core.
explanations.D: Opposite-answer trap. That Westfield County also expanded employment support during the same period actually weakens the Westfield County finding's reliability—but this functions more as an alternative explanation for Westfield's success than as a reason the program won't work in Hartley. Paradoxically, noting this confound could be seen as mildly undermining the advocate, but it is a weaker and less targeted attack than C.
explanations.E: Irrelevant / shift-in-subject trap. The fact that prior reform initiatives failed in Hartley County is consistent with the literacy program being different in kind and does not specifically address why this particular program would fail there.
